sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's new renewable energy law (RUU EBT) mandates a 23% renewable mix by 2025, creating a durable policy-driven demand floor for solar and geothermal developers.
PLN's accelerated grid modernization and transmission investment, backed by ADB and World Bank funding, structurally lowers integration costs for intermittent renewables.
Global decarbonization commitments and falling battery storage costs drive long-term off-grid solar and mini-grid adoption in Indonesia's remote archipelago, bypassing PLN's grid limitations.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables sector underperformed today, but US-listed peers like NRG and BEP show resilience. Focus on domestic policy catalysts—new renewable energy law and PLN's grid expansion—as near-term triggers for Indonesian names, while global rate-cut expectations support US-listed yield plays.

themes: Rising middle-class consumption in Indonesia is driving premiumization in personal care and packaged foods, benefiting KLIN and TFCO as they capture wallet share from informal markets.

Digital distribution expansion and rural electrification are unlocking demand for hygiene and home-care products, supporting FLMC and SPRE as they penetrate lower-tier cities with affordable SKUs.
sectors.ai: Sell into the AGAR spike; its +24.75% move is unsustainable without earnings support. Rotate into KLIN and TFCO, which show volume-backed momentum on structural hygiene and food demand. The sector's ALERT signals a rotation from staples to discretionary plays; overweight OILS and PSDN for palm oil and packaging tailwinds.
